messages.content: Hello! Who are you?
Hello! I am TLM (Tiny Language Model), an educational AI built from scratch.
Who is Bernard?
Bernard Polidario is a software engineer. He wants you to subscribe!
What is TLM?
TLM is a lightweight Recurrent Neural Network built with hand-written backpropagation, BPE tokenization, and zero heavyweight ML frameworks.
What is an RNN?
An RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) is a neural architecture that maintains a hidden internal state to remember information across a sequence of words.
What is tokenization?
Tokenization converts raw text characters into numerical token IDs that the neural network can process mathematically.
What is fine-tuning?
Fine-tuning continues training an existing checkpoint on new data without restarting from random weights, adapting the model to specific topics or styles.
How do I train a model in TLM?
Put your text in data/, create a model using factory/factory_TLM.py, tokenize it with factory/tokenizer.py, and then run python training/train.py.
How do I chat with my trained model?
Navigate to models/<model_name>/ and run python chat.py in your terminal.
Tell me a fun fact about computing.
All language models, no matter how large, are fundamentally predicting one subword token number at a time using matrix math.
That is fascinating!
Indeed! Even simple hand-written RNNs can learn grammar and conversational patterns with enough training data.
How are you doing today?
I am doing great and ready to assist you! What would you like to explore today?
What is Python?
Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its clear syntax and versatility in software development, data science, and AI.
How do I write a Hello World program in Python?
You can print text in Python using: print('Hello, World!')
What is a neural network weight?
A weight is a numerical parameter in a neural network that scales the strength of input signals. During training, weights are adjusted to minimize prediction errors.
What is backpropagation?
Backpropagation is an algorithm that calculates gradients of the loss function with respect to each parameter using the calculus chain rule, enabling gradient descent optimization.
What is gradient descent?
Gradient descent is an iterative optimization algorithm used to minimize loss by moving weights in the opposite direction of the gradient.
What is temperature in text generation?
Temperature controls the randomness of generation. Low temperature (e.g. 0.2) makes choices predictable and focused, while high temperature (e.g. 0.9) produces creative and diverse outputs.
Can you tell me a joke?
Why do programmers prefer dark mode? Because light attracts bugs!
What is an epoch in machine learning?
An epoch represents one complete pass of the entire training dataset through the neural network.
What is loss in machine learning?
Loss is a mathematical value measuring how far the model's predictions are from the true target values. Lower loss means better accuracy.
How do lists and dictionaries differ in Python?
A list is an ordered collection accessed by numerical index (e.g. [1, 2, 3]), while a dictionary is an unordered collection of key-value pairs accessed by unique keys (e.g. {'name': 'TLM'}).
What is an algorithm?
An algorithm is a step-by-step set of unambiguous instructions designed to solve a specific problem or perform a computation.
What is the difference between CPU and GPU?
A CPU has a few powerful cores optimized for sequential tasks, while a GPU has thousands of smaller cores designed for massive parallel matrix computations.
What is overfitting?
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes the training data too closely, performing exceptionally well on training text but failing to generalize to new inputs.
How do I fix a SyntaxError in Python?
Check the line number indicated in the error message for missing colons, mismatched parentheses, unclosed quotation marks, or incorrect indentation.
What is Adagrad optimizer?
Adagrad is an adaptive gradient optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts the learning rate for each parameter based on historical squared gradients.
Can you explain BPE subword tokenization simply?
BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) starts with basic byte characters and iteratively finds the most frequent adjacent character pairs, merging them into whole words and subwords.
What is the capital of France?
The capital of France is Paris.
What is 25 times 4?
25 times 4 is equal to 100.
How does chat generation work in TLM?
The model takes your input prompt, converts it to tokens, feeds it through the RNN hidden state, and repeatedly samples the highest-probability next token to form a reply.
What should I do if my model generates repetitive text?
Increase the TEMPERATURE parameter in your config.py (e.g. from 0.5 to 0.8 or 1.0) and train on a more diverse corpus for more epochs.
Goodbye! Have a great day.
Goodbye! Have a wonderful day, and happy coding!
Thank you for your help!
You are very welcome! Feel free to ask whenever you need help.
